# Testing gates

The gates every landing passes, over the tests [`testing`](../SKILL.md) classifies and the
builds [`testing-builds`](../builds/SKILL.md) describes.

## 1. Regressions

Every batch checks, formats and lints the workspace on the tree it lands, with warnings
denied, as [`toolchain`](../../../rust/toolchain/SKILL.md) describes, and tests what its
change can affect: its module and the modules that depend on it, as `modules.json` records
them, each by its tests' module paths.

Every build of those gates runs in the raw bindings' campaign mode, as
[`bindgen`](../../../rust/bindgen/SKILL.md)'s Build modes section describes, so that each fails when the
committed bindings do not match their input. A batch that changed the raw bindings, or a
landing that changes `c/`, also packages the safe crate, built alone in bundled mode from
the C it packages, with no build variant selected. Until the out-of-tree wrappers are
published, each crate the package depends on is patched to its local source, so that the
package builds alone.

The tests run against the matching variant, or a private replacement, and each event runs
them to its own depth:

- a batch: the tests above, plain and under ASan/UBSan, and its own tests under each other
  sanitizer its items call for, such as TSan where it asserts `Send` or `Sync` or adds a
  threaded callback, or MSan where C leaves memory it hands over partly unwritten;
- a wave's end: the workspace's tests, and the Miri gate below;
- a module's end, its switch in a port: every test under every available sanitizer,
  and BSan as below; and
- a ship point: every gate over the whole workspace under every available sanitizer, with
  the coverage measurement.
<!-- TODO: a wave's end and a module's end are run by the wave's last review batch and the
module pass, so a campaign without review runs neither: they need an owner there. -->

BSan, when available, is run for every batch and at module end:

- For a batch, it runs only on the individual tests or reproducers the batch expects to
  trigger it, each by exact name and alone; never on a whole test binary, a suite or the
  workspace.
- At module end, it runs as a gate over everything the module landed: the
  whole workspace, one invocation per test binary, as many side by side as
  [`concurrency`](../../../operations/concurrency/SKILL.md) describes, each under a `timeout`.

A batch runs the tests it wrote under Miri. Miri is also run after every wave, as a gate
over the whole workspace: one Miri run on the pinned nightly per test binary, the library's
and each integration suite's, as many side by side as
[`concurrency`](../../../operations/concurrency/SKILL.md) describes, each skipping the
compile-fail tests. The gate passes only
with no Miri error: a test that stops at the foreign boundary without the attribute gets
it, and any other Miri error is a UB candidate of the item it touches.

`end-gates`, beside this skill and documented by its `--help`, runs a wave's and a
module's end gates so, over a snapshot of the tree, so that work goes on in the tree while
they run: the workspace under each variant, Miri and BSan per test binary, and the BSan
tests known never to finish skipped by name, each skip checked against its binary's test
list before anything runs.

Each gate run starts in the background and is waited on to exit; its output is neither
polled nor read while it runs. BSan reports false positives at the foreign boundary, so
only a true positive, a report that reproduces through the Rust side as a single test or
standalone reproducer, becomes a UB finding.

Every translation and review batch measures the consumer-facing API of its items against
the tip it rebased onto, each change classified as the dashboard's API stability columns
name them. An item's API is fixed by its first landing: a later landing
that changes or removes it, a port, a later stage, a rebind or a review fix alike, breaks
its consumers, and is kept only with its reason recorded in the batch's notes, such as a
soundness fix; the measure does not fail the gate. A module's integration measures every
item of the module against the module's base, and a ship point the whole crate against the
previous ship point.

When C changed, the configured C build and baseline run. A wrap-only batch with no C
change does not need the full C baseline.

A batch validates its own change on its own base first. Its rebase onto the integration
branch, under the landing lock that [`versioning`](../../../operations/versioning/SKILL.md)'s Landing section
describes, then combines that change with the work landed since: the gates run again are
those that could catch a regression the combination introduces, judged from what the
batch's change and the rebased-in changes touch and how they could interact. A gate that
neither side's changes could affect keeps the result it had, and a rebase that conflicts
makes the resolved tree new work of the batch's own.

A `port` batch changes no C: its gates are those above, run against the variants with its
module's export feature off, so that the ported Rust is tested beside the C it replaces.
It also checks and lints the safe crate with that feature on, which compiles the module's
gateway without linking it, and each export is checked at compile time against the raw
binding of the C declaration it replaces, so that a signature that drifts from C's fails
to build.

A module's switch removes its translation unit, and the C tests tied to it that reach
its internals, from `c/`, rebuilds the variants from the C that remains and deletes the
module's export feature, as
[`porting-workflow`](../../../workflows/porting-workflow/SKILL.md)'s Builds section
describes. Its gates are a module's end's, in campaign mode over the rebuilt variants, and
the target's remaining C tests, which link the remaining C and the safe crate's Rust static
library, so that the C reaches the ported module through its exports: the module's tied C
tests that use only its public API among them, as the porting workflow's Tests follow
their modules section describes. Before a tied C test leaves, the cases none of the
module's `unit_pub` tests carries over are listed, as [`testing`](../SKILL.md)'s C tests
carried over section describes.

   discarding either side. No merge is committed while its tree holds a conflict marker,
   here or wherever a branch takes another by merge, such as a wave's branch taking the
   working branch, so that every branch forked from it starts from a tree that builds.
2. The merge's tree passes the gates of
   [`testing-gates`](../../verification/testing/gates/SKILL.md)'s Regressions section, and in
   a port campaign, in the run that holds the last wave of the module's `wrap` and `port`
   items, the module's switch from C to Rust, which happens once, as
   [`porting-workflow`](../../workflows/porting-workflow/SKILL.md)'s Builds section describes:
   its export feature is deleted, and the C test cases none of its `unit_pub` tests carries
   over are listed before its C tests leave.
3. The working branch is fast-forwarded to the module's branch.

Modules integrate one at a time, and nothing else is committed on the working branch while
one does, so that its fast-forward cannot be rejected. A port's later-stage waves come after
their module's switch, are promoted to the working branch, and integrate nothing, as
the porting workflow's Later stages section describes.

## 6. Identity

Every commit of a campaign, in its repository and its wrappers', is authored and committed
as Crustify, whose GitHub account is `crustify-ai` and whose git identity is
`crustify <crustify@berkeley.edu>`, whatever the repository's git configuration says,
unless the settings' `identity` answer names another: an author and any co-authors, each
as `Name <email>`. The author named there then authors and commits every commit, and each
message ends with one `Co-Authored-By:` trailer per co-author and no other, none that an
agent's host suggests included.

The identity is passed explicitly, as configuration on the command line, to every command
that writes a commit, a rebase, a merge and a cherry-pick as much as a commit, since the
host may have no git identity of its own.

name: testing-gates
description: "The regression gates work lands through, by event: a batch's scoped gates, a wave's, a module's end or switch from C and a ship point's; campaign mode and packaging, sanitizers, BSan and Miri, rebases under the landing lock, and a port batch's export checks. Read before running a batch's gates, landing, integrating a module or shipping."

# Testing gates

The gates every landing passes, over the tests [`testing`](../SKILL.md) classifies and the
builds [`testing-builds`](../builds/SKILL.md) describes.

## 1. Regressions

Every batch checks, formats and lints the workspace on the tree it lands, with warnings
denied, as [`toolchain`](../../../rust/toolchain/SKILL.md) describes, and tests what its
change can affect: its module and the modules that depend on it, as `modules.json` records
them, each by its tests' module paths.

Every build of those gates runs in the raw bindings' campaign mode, as
[`bindgen`](../../../rust/bindgen/SKILL.md)'s Build modes section describes, so that each fails when the
committed bindings do not match their input. A batch that changed the raw bindings, or a
landing that changes `c/`, also packages the safe crate, built alone in bundled mode from
the C it packages, with no build variant selected. Until the out-of-tree wrappers are
published, each crate the package depends on is patched to its local source, so that the
package builds alone.

The tests run against the matching variant, or a private replacement, and each event runs
them to its own depth:

- a batch: the tests above, plain and under ASan/UBSan, and its own tests under each other
  sanitizer its items call for, such as TSan where it asserts `Send` or `Sync` or adds a
  threaded callback, or MSan where C leaves memory it hands over partly unwritten;
- a wave's end: the workspace's tests, and the Miri gate below;
- a module's end, its switch in a port: every test under every available sanitizer,
  and BSan as below; and
- a ship point: every gate over the whole workspace under every available sanitizer, with
  the coverage measurement.
<!-- TODO: a wave's end and a module's end are run by the wave's last review batch and the
module pass, so a campaign without review runs neither: they need an owner there. -->

BSan, when available, is run for every batch and at module end:

- For a batch, it runs only on the individual tests or reproducers the batch expects to
  trigger it, each by exact name and alone; never on a whole test binary, a suite or the
  workspace.
- At module end, it runs as a gate over everything the module landed: the
  whole workspace, one invocation per test binary, as many side by side as
  [`concurrency`](../../../operations/concurrency/SKILL.md) describes, each under a `timeout`.

A batch runs the tests it wrote under Miri. Miri is also run after every wave, as a gate
over the whole workspace: one Miri run on the pinned nightly per test binary, the library's
and each integration suite's, as many side by side as
[`concurrency`](../../../operations/concurrency/SKILL.md) describes, each skipping the
compile-fail tests. The gate passes only
with no Miri error: a test that stops at the foreign boundary without the attribute gets
it, and any other Miri error is a UB candidate of the item it touches.

`end-gates`, beside this skill and documented by its `--help`, runs a wave's and a
module's end gates so, over a snapshot of the tree, so that work goes on in the tree while
they run: the workspace under each variant, Miri and BSan per test binary, and the BSan
tests known never to finish skipped by name, each skip checked against its binary's test
list before anything runs.

Each gate run starts in the background and is waited on to exit; its output is neither
polled nor read while it runs. BSan reports false positives at the foreign boundary, so
only a true positive, a report that reproduces through the Rust side as a single test or
standalone reproducer, becomes a UB finding.

Every translation and review batch measures the consumer-facing API of its items against
the tip it rebased onto, each change classified as the dashboard's API stability columns
name them. An item's API is fixed by its first landing: a later landing
that changes or removes it, a port, a later stage, a rebind or a review fix alike, breaks
its consumers, and is kept only with its reason recorded in the batch's notes, such as a
soundness fix; the measure does not fail the gate. A module's integration measures every
item of the module against the module's base, and a ship point the whole crate against the
previous ship point.

When C changed, the configured C build and baseline run. A wrap-only batch with no C
change does not need the full C baseline.

A batch validates its own change on its own base first. Its rebase onto the integration
branch, under the landing lock that [`versioning`](../../../operations/versioning/SKILL.md)'s Landing section
describes, then combines that change with the work landed since: the gates run again are
those that could catch a regression the combination introduces, judged from what the
batch's change and the rebased-in changes touch and how they could interact. A gate that
neither side's changes could affect keeps the result it had, and a rebase that conflicts
makes the resolved tree new work of the batch's own.

A `port` batch changes no C: its gates are those above, run against the variants with its
module's export feature off, so that the ported Rust is tested beside the C it replaces.
It also checks and lints the safe crate with that feature on, which compiles the module's
gateway without linking it, and each export is checked at compile time against the raw
binding of the C declaration it replaces, so that a signature that drifts from C's fails
to build.

A module's switch removes its translation unit, and the C tests tied to it that reach
its internals, from `c/`, rebuilds the variants from the C that remains and deletes the
module's export feature, as
[`porting-workflow`](../../../workflows/porting-workflow/SKILL.md)'s Builds section
describes. Its gates are a module's end's, in campaign mode over the rebuilt variants, and
the target's remaining C tests, which link the remaining C and the safe crate's Rust static
library, so that the C reaches the ported module through its exports: the module's tied C
tests that use only its public API among them, as the porting workflow's Tests follow
their modules section describes. Before a tied C test leaves, the cases none of the
module's `unit_pub` tests carries over are listed, as [`testing`](../SKILL.md)'s C tests
carried over section describes.

#!/bin/bash
# Build a generation of the target's variants from the C that remains (crustify's setup
# skill, Builds; porting-workflow, Builds): run after a module's switch removes C, and
# whenever the shared variants are rebuilt.
#
#   build-variants.sh <generation dir> [<variant>...]
#
# A generation is a directory beside crustify/builds, as crustify/builds.gen<n>, which a
# checkout's crustify/builds links to once it is built: it holds `c`, a detached worktree
# of this checkout's `c/` repository at the commit `c/` has checked out, which `c/` must
# hold without changes, and one build dir per variant of crustify/artifacts/build.json
# (every one by default), named as its `dir` names it. Each variant's `configure` and
# `build` commands run from its dir, physically resolved, so that the relative paths they
# take (the generation's `../c`, the side campaigns' installs four levels up) resolve as
# for the shared builds, with CRUSTIFY_ROOT set to this checkout, whose scripts the
# commands run and whose Rust the C consumers link. The variants build side by side, each
# logging to <dir>/crustify/build.log; the exit status is 1 when any fails, naming it.
# An existing generation is not rebuilt: a variant whose dir exists is refused.
set -euo pipefail
usage='usage: build-variants.sh <generation dir> [<variant>...]'
gen=${1:?$usage}
shift
root=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)
spec=$root/crustify/artifacts/build.json
mapfile -t all < <(python3 -I -c 'import json,sys; print("\n".join(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["variants"]))' "$spec")
variants=("$@")
[ ${#variants[@]} -gt 0 ] || variants=("${all[@]}")
for v in "${variants[@]}"; do
  printf '%s\n' "${all[@]}" | grep -qx -- "$v" || { echo "build-variants.sh: no variant $v in $spec" >&2; exit 2; }
done

mkdir -p "$gen"
gen=$(cd -P "$gen" && pwd)

#!/bin/bash
# Run cargo against one crustify prebuild of libgit2, instrumenting Rust to match.
#
#   crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh <variant> <cargo subcommand> [args...]
#
# <variant> is a `variants` key of crustify/artifacts/build.json: plain, coverage, asan-ubsan,
# tsan or bsan. Each variant uses its own target dir under target/.
# The safe crate's build script, in campaign mode, links the variant's static archive (its
# `static` in build.json) into each test binary, so the C runs under the instrumentation the
# Rust is built with here, one runtime serving both. Set CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR to a private build
# of the variant, which carries the same archive, to link it instead of the shared one.
set -euo pipefail
variant=${1:?usage: cargo-variant.sh <variant> <cargo subcommand> [args...]}
shift
here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)
host=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
export CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT=$variant
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=${CARGO_TARGET_DIR:-$here/target/$variant}
# pcre2-sys links the variant's side-campaign PCRE2, the one libgit2's C links, rather than
# building its vendored copy, which would shadow it in every test binary. The side campaigns'
# clones sit where the variant's build found their installs, beside the repository whose
# crustify/builds holds it (build.json's configure takes them from `$PWD/../../../..` in
# crustify/builds/<variant>): resolved physically through crustify/builds, which a worktree or
# a gate snapshot links to that repository's, so that every checkout finds the same ones.
side=$(realpath -m "$here/crustify/builds/$variant/../../../..")
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$side/pcre2-bindings/crustify/builds/$variant/install/lib/pkgconfig${PKG_CONFIG_PATH:+:$PKG_CONFIG_PATH}"
cd "$here"
# The nightly the workspace pins, for the sanitizers that need it.
nightly=$(sed -n 's/^nightly = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' Cargo.toml)
# Cargo's own flags must come before a `--`, which hands the rest to the test binaries.
pre=() post=()
for arg in "$@"; do
  if [ ${#post[@]} -gt 0 ] || [ "$arg" = -- ]; then post+=("$arg"); else pre+=("$arg"); fi
done
case $variant in
  plain)
    exec cargo "$@" ;;
  coverage)
    # Source-based coverage on the pinned nightly, against the variant's clang-instrumented C,
    # which each test binary links statically, so that rustc's profiler runtime counts both;
    # crustify/scripts/coverage/ measures the suites as the testing spec's Coverage section does.
    export RUSTFLAGS="${RUSTFLAGS:-} -C instrument-coverage"
    export RUSTDOCFLAGS="${RUSTDOCFLAGS:-} -C instrument-coverage"
    export LLVM_PROFILE_FILE=${LLVM_PROFILE_FILE:-$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/profraw/%p-%m.profraw}

    export RUSTDOCFLAGS="${RUSTDOCFLAGS:-} -Zsanitizer=address"
    export ASAN_OPTIONS=${ASAN_OPTIONS:-detect_leaks=1:abort_on_error=1}
    export UBSAN_OPTIONS=${UBSAN_OPTIONS:-print_stacktrace=1:halt_on_error=1}
    exec cargo "+$nightly" "${pre[@]}" --target $host "${post[@]}" ;;

    export RUSTDOCFLAGS="${RUSTDOCFLAGS:-} -Zsanitizer=thread"

    export TSAN_OPTIONS=${TSAN_OPTIONS:-halt_on_error=1:suppressions=$here/crustify/scripts/tsan.supp}

http.c: switch from C to Rust (modules/libgit2/deps/llhttp/http.c/integration/run-1)

deps/llhttp/http.c is the fourth module to switch, and llhttp's second:
its export feature, ffi-export-deps-llhttp-http-c, is deleted, so that
http.rs's gateway, with its four unit_priv tests, compiles from now on,
and the fork's main drops the TU (c/ at 230c9dbdb, `integrate
deps/llhttp/http.c`). llhttp.c's generated parser reaches the three
hooks, llhttp__before_headers_complete, llhttp__after_headers_complete
and llhttp__after_message_complete, and libgit2's HTTP client
(httpparser.h's git_http_parser_keep_alive, which httpclient.c expands)
llhttp_should_keep_alive, through the exports, in the crate's static
library the C already links (LIBGIT2_RUST_LIBRARY). llhttp.h stays, for
llhttp.c and the HTTP client. headers_code loses its dead_code
expectation, which named the feature: the gateway now uses it always.

The module's six equivalence tests, which need the C, are retired
(tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/http.rs and its mod line), each mapped to the
unit tests that keep its behaviour by the module pass (wave-197/batch-1's
equiv-retirement.md). Every one of them calls C, http.c's own or
llhttp.c's parse, and carries the Miri `calls C` marker, so none is
carried over. The raw binding of llhttp_should_keep_alive stays and
reaches its export; that of llhttp_message_needs_eof, which has no
export and which only http.c's C and its equivalence tests called, goes
with its allowlist entry. The hooks have no header declaration and no
raw binding.

Co-Authored-By: crustify <crustify@berkeley.edu>
EOF

content.content:
#!/bin/bash
# Drive libgit2's HTTP client through a variant's own C, over a smart-HTTP remote on localhost
# (crustify's testing-gates skill, Regressions: a module's switch, for a module whose exports
# the HTTP client reaches, which no offline C test does; crustify/evolution/module-switch-procedure).
#
#   http-gate.sh <variant dir> <out dir>
#
# <variant dir> is a built variant, crustify/builds.gen<n>/<variant>, with its `git2` and
# `libgit2_tests`; nothing is written into it. Two remotes are started from
# crustify/scripts/http-remote.py over scratch repositories under <out dir>/remotes, one open
# and one asking for Basic credentials (foo:bar), each serving every framing it offers
# (Content-Length, chunked, chunked with extensions, close-delimited, malformed):
#
# 1. the variant's `git2 clone` of testrepo.git (c/tests/resources) and of a three-commit
#    repository of the generation's c/ tree at a fixed commit, through the Content-Length and
#    chunked framings, and clones that fail: through the close-delimited framing, which
#    libgit2 does not read to its end, through a response llhttp refuses, of a missing
#    repository (404), and of the guarded remote without credentials (401); each clone's exit
#    status, refs, HEAD, checked-out tree and `git fsck --connectivity-only` outcome, or its
#    error;
# 2. the variant's `libgit2_tests -sonline::push -sonline::clone::credentials`, libgit2's own
#    C tests of a push and a clone over GITTEST_REMOTE_URL, against the guarded remote with
#    foo:bar, through the Content-Length and chunked framings: its TAP tally.
#
# <out dir>/results.txt is one line per case, free of times, ports and paths, so that two
# generations' results compare with `diff`; every process's output is kept beside it, and each
# line counts the sanitizer reports that process printed (`reports=`). The exit status is 0
# when every clone that should succeed did and every suite passed, 1 otherwise.
set -uo pipefail
usage='usage: http-gate.sh <variant dir> <out dir>'
d=$(cd -P "${1:?$usage}" && pwd) || exit 2
out=${2:?$usage}
here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
c=$(cd -P "$d/../c" && pwd) || { echo "http-gate.sh: no generation c/ beside $d" >&2; exit 2; }
[ -x "$d/git2" ] && [ -x "$d/libgit2_tests" ] || { echo "http-gate.sh: $d has no git2 or libgit2_tests" >&2; exit 2; }
rm -rf "$out"
mkdir -p "$out"
out=$(cd -P "$out" && pwd)
export LLVM_PROFILE_FILE=${LLVM_PROFILE_FILE:-/dev/null}
export GIT_AUTHOR_DATE='2026-01-01T00:00:00Z' GIT_COMMITTER_DATE='2026-01-01T00:00:00Z'
# big.git's tree: the campaign's source revision, which every generation's c/ holds.
big_tip=0551dfd4a
framings=(length chunked chunked-ext)
status=0
results=$out/results.txt
: >"$results"
reports() { grep -cE 'WARNING: ThreadSanitizer|ERROR: AddressSanitizer|ERROR: LeakSanitizer|runtime error:' "$@" 2>/dev/null | awk -F: '{s+=$NF} END {print s+0}'; }

# The remotes' repositories.
r=$out/remotes
mkdir -p "$r/open" "$r/guarded"
git clone -q --bare "$c/tests/resources/testrepo.git" "$r/open/testrepo.git"
# big.git: the source revision's tree as three commits, the second removing src/ and the
# third restoring it, each with a fixed author and date, so that its ids are every run's.
mkdir -p "$r/src"
git -C "$c" archive "$big_tip" | tar -x -C "$r/src"
(
  cd "$r/src" && git init -q -b main . &&
    export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=crustify GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=crustify@berkeley.edu \
      GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=crustify GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=crustify@berkeley.edu &&
clone testrepo-length rc=0 refs=74a9a6c1e979d0a4 head=a65fedf39aefe402d3bb6e24df4d4f5fe4547750 status=e3b0c44298fc1c14 fsck=ok reports=0

#!/bin/bash
# Run the target's remaining C tests over a variant's build and compare them with the C test
# baseline (crustify's testing-gates skill, Regressions: a module's switch; setup, Baseline).
#
#   c-tests.sh <variant dir> <out dir> [jobs]
#
# <variant dir> is a built variant, crustify/builds/<variant>, whose C tests link the safe
# crate's Rust static library; its name is the variant whose record of
# crustify/artifacts/c-baseline.json the run is compared with. Nothing is written into it:
# every output goes under <out dir>.
#
# 1. build.json's `test` command, `ctest --output-on-failure -R '^(offline|util)$'`, over a
#    copy of the variant's CTestTestfile.cmake tree, so that ctest's own records stay out of
#    the variant, beside the suites of step 2: <out dir>/ctest.log, its exit status in
#    <out dir>/ctest.rc.
# 2. Every offline libgit2_tests suite and every util_tests suite alone, <jobs> side by side
#    (default 8), each under a 30-minute timeout, as the baseline ran them: TAP output in
#    <out dir>/suites/<binary>/<suite>.{tap,err,rc}. `online::*` suites need the network and
#    are left out, as the `offline` ctest target leaves them.
# 3. The tally, <out dir>/tally.json (cases passed, failed and skipped, and every suite that
#    failed a case or exited non-zero, with the sanitizer reports it printed), compared with
#    the baseline's record: the exit status is 0 when the case counts and the non-zero suites
#    (binary, suite, exit status) match it, and 1 otherwise, naming each difference. ctest's
#    status is reported beside it; under TSan the baseline's own races fail `offline`.
#
# The coverage variant's profiles go to /dev/null unless LLVM_PROFILE_FILE says otherwise.
set -uo pipefail
usage='usage: c-tests.sh <variant dir> <out dir> [jobs]'
d=$(cd -P "${1:?$usage}" && pwd) || exit 2
out=${2:?$usage}
jobs=${3:-8}
here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
variant=$(basename "$d")
[ -x "$d/libgit2_tests" ] && [ -x "$d/util_tests" ] || { echo "c-tests.sh: $d has no C tests built" >&2; exit 2; }
mkdir -p "$out"
out=$(cd -P "$out" && pwd)
export LLVM_PROFILE_FILE=${LLVM_PROFILE_FILE:-/dev/null}

# 1. ctest, over a copy of the test files: they name the executables by absolute path.
rm -rf "$out/ctest"

end-gates: run a wave's or a module's end gates over a snapshot of a tree.

    end-gates <tree> --logs <dir> [--stages plain,asan-ubsan,tsan,miri,bsan]
              [--rev <rev> | --working-tree] [--package <name>] [--runner <cmd>]
              [--link <path>]... [--skip-file <file>] [--stage-env <stage>:<K>=<V>]...
              [--timeout <seconds>] [--parallel <n>] [--nightly <toolchain>]

The gates of testing-gates' Regressions section, run exactly so:

1. The tree's commit (`--rev`, HEAD by default), or its working tree with
   `--working-tree`, is copied to a snapshot, `<tree>/crustify/tmp/gates-<label>`, so that
   work goes on in the tree while the gates run. Each submodule, and each `--link` path
   (such as the variants' builds dir), is symlinked from the tree into it, and the snapshot
   is made a git repository, since a test may discover the repository it runs in.
2. Each skip of `--skip-file` is checked against its test binary's `--list` before any
   stage runs: a skip that names no test, or that would also skip another, since libtest
   skips by substring, fails the run.
3. The stages run in the order given:
   - a variant (`plain` and each sanitizer but `bsan`): the workspace's tests,
     `<runner> <variant> test --workspace --no-fail-fast`, with that stage's skips;
   - `miri`: the package's test binaries built once on the pinned nightly, then one
     `cargo miri test` per test binary, side by side, each skipping `compile_fail`;
   - `bsan`: the test binaries built once, then one invocation per test binary, side by
     side, each under `--timeout`, with that stage's skips.
4. Each run writes `<logs>/<stage>[-<binary>].log`; `<logs>/summary.json` and
   `summary.txt` record each run's command, exit status, duration, test-result lines and
   failed tests. A run that exceeds its timeout reports `timed_out`.

The skip file holds one skip per line, `<stage> <binary> <exact test name>`, the binary
being `lib` or an integration test's name; `#` starts a comment. A variant stage's skips
apply to every binary of the workspace.

The job count is the environment's: `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS` for builds, `RUST_TEST_THREADS` for
each binary's tests, as concurrency describes. The exit status is 0 when every run
passed, 1 when any failed, and 2 when the run could not start.

Standard library only.

  --rev REV             the commit to snapshot (default: HEAD)
  --working-tree        snapshot the working tree, tracked and untracked files

  --label LABEL         the snapshot's name under crustify/tmp (default: the

  --package PACKAGE     the package whose test binaries run per binary

  --runner RUNNER       the command that runs cargo against a variant, given

git clone -q --bare "$c/tests/resources/testrepo.git" "$r/guarded/testrepo.git"

python3 -I "$here/http-remote.py" "$r/open" "$out/open.port" --log "$out/open.log" 2>"$out/open.err" &

python3 -I "$here/http-remote.py" "$r/guarded" "$out/guarded.port" --auth foo:bar --log "$out/guarded.log" 2>"$out/guarded.err" &
pids+=($!)
for _ in $(seq 100); do [ -s "$out/open.port" ] && [ -s "$out/guarded.port" ] && break; sleep 0.1; done
open=http://127.0.0.1:$(cat "$out/open.port")
guarded=http://127.0.0.1:$(cat "$out/guarded.port")

# 1. The CLI's clones. <expect> is ok or fail.
clone() {
  local name=$1 url=$2 expect=$3 dir=$out/clones/$1
  mkdir -p "$out/clones"
  (cd "$out/clones" && timeout 600 "$d/git2" clone "$url" "$dir" >"$dir.out" 2>"$dir.err" </dev/null)
  local rc=$?
  local line="clone $name rc=$rc"
  if [ $rc -eq 0 ] && [ -d "$dir/.git" ]; then
    local refs head tree fsck
    refs=$(git -C "$dir" for-each-ref --format='%(objectname) %(refname)' | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)
    head=$(git -C "$dir" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null)
    tree=$(git -C "$dir" status --porcelain --untracked-files=all | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)
    git -C "$dir" fsck --connectivity-only --no-progress >"$dir.fsck" 2>&1 && fsck=ok || fsck=failed
    line+=" refs=$refs head=$head status=$tree fsck=$fsck"
  else
    line+=" error=\"$(grep -v '^\s*$' "$dir.err" | grep -vE 'Sanitizer|^ +#|^SUMMARY|^==' | tail -1)\""
  fi
  line+=" reports=$(reports "$dir.err")"
  echo "$line" >>"$results"
  case $expect in
    ok) [ $rc -eq 0 ] && [[ $line == *fsck=ok* ]] || status=1 ;;
    fail) [ $rc -ne 0 ] || status=1 ;;
  esac
}
for f in "${framings[@]}"; do
  clone "testrepo-$f" "$open/$f/testrepo.git" ok
  clone "big-$f" "$open/$f/big.git" ok
done
clone testrepo-close "$open/close/testrepo.git" fail
clone testrepo-malformed "$open/malformed/testrepo.git" fail
clone missing "$open/length/missing.git" fail
clone unauthorised "$guarded/length/testrepo.git" fail

# 2. libgit2's own online tests of a push and a clone.
for f in "${framings[@]}"; do
  s=$out/suites/$f
  mkdir -p "$s/tmp"
  (cd "$s" && TMPDIR=$s/tmp GITTEST_REMOTE_URL="$guarded/$f/push-$f.git" GITTEST_REMOTE_USER=foo \
    GITTEST_REMOTE_PASS=bar timeout 1800 "$d/libgit2_tests" -t -sonline::push \
    -sonline::clone::credentials >"$s/tap" 2>"$s/err" </dev/null)
  rc=$?
  ok=$(grep -c '^ok ' "$s/tap") notok=$(grep -c '^not ok ' "$s/tap") skip=$(grep -c '# SKIP' "$s/tap")
  echo "suites $f rc=$rc ok=$ok not_ok=$notok skip=$skip reports=$(reports "$s/err" "$s/tap")" >>"$results"
  [ $rc -eq 0 ] && [ "$notok" -eq 0 ] && [ "$ok" -gt 0 ] || status=1
done

# The requests the remotes answered, by method, framing and status; the connections a client
# reset or closed mid-request (`error` lines) depend on timing, and stay in the logs alone.
for side in open guarded; do
  grep -v '^error ' "$out/$side.log" | sed -E 's/\?.*( [0-9]+)$/\1/' | awk -v s="$side" '{split($2, p, "/"); print "requests " s " " $1 " " p[2] " " $3}' |
    sort | uniq -c | awk '{print $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, "count=" $1}' >>"$results"
done
cat "$results"
exit $status

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""A smart-HTTP Git remote on localhost, for the C that drives libgit2's HTTP client.

    http-remote.py <root> <port file> [--auth USER:PASS] [--log FILE]

Serves the repositories under <root> through `git http-backend`, upload-pack and
receive-pack both, over HTTP/1.1 with persistent connections, so that libgit2's HTTP
client (src/libgit2/transports/httpclient.c over httpparser.c and llhttp) reads several
responses on one connection. It listens on 127.0.0.1 at a port the system picks, written to
<port file> once it accepts connections, and runs until killed.

The first component of a request's path picks how the response's body is framed, the rest
naming the repository under <root>, so that one remote serves every framing llhttp parses:

- `/length/<repo>`: a `Content-Length` body;
- `/chunked/<repo>`: `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, in chunks of 1, 7, 4096 and 65536 bytes
  in turn, so that a chunk's size line, its data and its end fall across reads;
- `/chunked-ext/<repo>`: chunked as above, every size line carrying chunk extensions
  (`;a=b;flag;q="x y"`), which llhttp's chunk-extension callbacks are called for;
- `/close/<repo>`: no length and no chunking, the body ending with the connection
  (`Connection: close`).
- `/malformed/<repo>`: a response whose header block llhttp refuses, a space in a header's
  name, so that the client reports the parser's error and its reason.

With `--auth`, every request without that user's Basic credentials is answered 401 with a
`WWW-Authenticate: Basic` challenge, a body and the connection kept, before the backend
runs. A path that names no repository is the backend's 404. Requests are logged to
`--log`, one line each, method, path and status, for the caller to compare.

Crustify's campaign check of a module whose exports libgit2's HTTP client reaches, at its
switch from C (crustify/evolution/module-switch-procedure): run it with `python3 -I`.
"""

import base64
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

CHUNKS = (1, 7, 4096, 65536)
FRAMINGS = ("length", "chunked", "chunked-ext", "close", "malformed")


def main(argv):
    args = list(argv)
    auth = log = None
    while "--auth" in args or "--log" in args:
        for flag in ("--auth", "--log"):
            if flag in args:
                i = args.index(flag)
                value = args[i + 1]
                del args[i : i + 2]
                if flag == "--auth":
                    auth = value
                else:
                    log = value
    if len(args) != 2:
        sys.exit(__doc__.split("\n\n")[1])
    root, port_file = os.path.realpath(args[0]), args[1]
    log_lock = threading.Lock()
    log_file = open(log, "a", buffering=1) if log else None
    expected = "Basic " + base64.b64encode(auth.encode()).decode() if auth else None

    class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
        protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"

        def log_message(self, fmt, *a):
            pass

        def record(self, status):
            if log_file:
                with log_lock:
                    log_file.write(f"{self.command} {self.path} {status}\n")

        def read_body(self):
            if self.headers.get("Transfer-Encoding", "").lower() == "chunked":
                body = bytearray()
                while True:
                    size = int(self.rfile.readline().split(b";")[0].strip(), 16)
                    if size == 0:
                        while self.rfile.readline() not in (b"\r\n", b"\n", b""):
                            pass
                        return bytes(body)
                    body += self.rfile.read(size)
                    self.rfile.readline()
            return self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0))

        def send(self, status, headers, body, framing):
            self.send_response(status)
            for k, v in headers:
                self.send_header(k, v)
            if framing == "malformed":
                self.wfile.write(b"HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nBad Header: x\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\n\r\n")
                self.wfile.flush()
                self.close_connection = True
                return
            if framing == "length":
                self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
                self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write(body)
            elif framing == "close":
                self.send_header("Connection", "close")
                self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write(body)
                self.close_connection = True
            else:
                self.send_header("Transfer-Encoding", "chunked")
                self.end_headers()
                ext = ';a=b;flag;q="x y"' if framing == "chunked-ext" else ""
                pos, i = 0, 0
                while pos < len(body):
                    n = CHUNKS[i % len(CHUNKS)]
                    piece = body[pos : pos + n]
                    self.wfile.write(b"%x%s\r\n%s\r\n" % (len(piece), ext.encode(), piece))
                    pos, i = pos + n, i + 1
                self.wfile.write(b"0%s\r\n\r\n" % ext.encode())
            self.wfile.flush()

        def serve(self):
            body = self.read_body() if self.command == "POST" else b""
            path, _, query = self.path.partition("?")
            framing, _, rest = path.lstrip("/").partition("/")
            if framing not in FRAMINGS:
                framing, rest = "length", path.lstrip("/")
            if expected and self.headers.get("Authorization") != expected:
                self.record(401)
                self.send(
                    401,
                    [("WWW-Authenticate", 'Basic realm="crustify"'),
                     ("Content-Type", "text/plain")],
                    b"authentication required\n",
                    framing,
                )
                return
            env = {
                "PATH": os.environ.get("PATH", "/usr/bin:/bin"),
                "GIT_PROJECT_ROOT": root,
                "GIT_HTTP_EXPORT_ALL": "1",
                "PATH_INFO": "/" + rest,
                "QUERY_STRING": query,
                "REQUEST_METHOD": self.command,
                "CONTENT_TYPE": self.headers.get("Content-Type", ""),
                "CONTENT_LENGTH": str(len(body)),
                "REMOTE_USER": auth.split(":")[0] if auth else "anonymous",
                "REMOTE_ADDR": "127.0.0.1",
                "SERVER_PROTOCOL": "HTTP/1.1",
                "GIT_CONFIG_COUNT": "1",
                "GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0": "http.receivepack",
                "GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0": "true",
            }
            if self.headers.get("Git-Protocol"):
                env["GIT_PROTOCOL"] = self.headers["Git-Protocol"]
            out = subprocess.run(
                ["git", "http-backend"], input=body, env=env, capture_output=True
            ).stdout
            head, _, payload = out.partition(b"\r\n\r\n")
            if not _:
                head, _, payload = out.partition(b"\n\n")
            status, headers = 200, []
            for line in head.decode("latin-1").splitlines():
                k, _, v = line.partition(":")
                if k.lower() == "status":
                    status = int(v.split()[0])
                elif k:
                    headers.append((k, v.strip()))
            self.record(status)
            self.send(status, headers, payload, framing)

        do_GET = do_POST = serve

    class Server(ThreadingHTTPServer):
        daemon_threads = True

        def handle_error(self, request, client_address):
            # A client that gives up on a request, as libgit2 does on an error, resets or
            # closes its connection: logged, not printed.
            exc = sys.exc_info()[1]
            if log_file:
                with log_lock:
                    log_file.write(f"error {type(exc).__name__}\n")

    server = Server(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
    tmp = port_file + ".tmp"
    with open(tmp, "w") as f:
        f.write(f"{server.server_address[1]}\n")
    os.replace(tmp, port_file)
    server.serve_forever()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1:])

and its `equiv`, `ub_safe` and `unit_pub` files, for every objective with `fix`, and the wave's
and the module's end gates. `llhttp.rs`'s accessors and api.c's `execute` were read, not
reported on. It files one finding, `+misc`, fixed.

- **misc**: the tree batch 0 landed fails `clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`,
  with the export feature off and on, in its own tests. Its notes record the gate as passing.
  `unit_pub`'s `after_headers_complete_on_a_zeroed_parser` trips `too_many_lines` and
  `type_complexity`, and `equiv`'s `State::parser` the denied `multiple_unsafe_ops_per_block`.
  The case tuple is now the alias `HeadersCase`, read by the helper
  `assert_after_headers_complete`, and the fixture reads and writes in two justified blocks.
  The workspace then formats and lints clean, with the feature off and on.

What held. The five methods are http.c's bodies branch for branch: the type and method
compared as llhttp's enums, `upgrade` read as C's nonzero byte and written `0` or `1` (which
`llhttp.c`'s `is_equal_upgrade` compares with `1`), `finish` set to `HTTP_FINISH_SAFE`'s byte,
the flags cleared. The exports keep what `llhttp.c`'s generated parser relies on. Each hook
returns the codes its `switch` goes on from: `after_headers_complete` 0 to 5,
`after_message_complete` `1` to keep the connection, else `0`, `before_headers_complete` `0`.
Each is checked at compile time against `llhttp.c`'s prototypes, writes only what C's wrote,
and never unwinds: a panic, or the NULL C never passes, aborts. Their handles are ffibox's
pointer handles. A hook's `ParserMut` lives for the call, inside the parse whose own handle
is not used meanwhile, and the `parser_mut` and `llhttp_should_keep_alive` contracts hold for
every caller: `reason` is only ever one of `llhttp.c`'s literals or a `&'static CStr`. libgit2's
HTTP client reads `llhttp_should_keep_alive` as a boolean. The kept `HTTP/2.0` departure is no
`logic` finding: RFC 9112's "HTTP/1.1 (or later)" speaks of HTTP/1's syntax, which a `2.0` start
line does not follow, and closing is the conservative reading. It now has a named unit test.
`gateway-feature-across-a-multiline-attribute`'s reproducer transcribes `build.rs`'s
`gateway_lines` faithfully, and still reproduces. One thing for the switch: deleting the
feature leaves `headers_code`'s `cfg_attr(not(any(test, feature = …)), expect(dead_code))`
naming a feature that no longer exists. Clippy with warnings denied then fails on the unknown
`cfg` and the unmet expectation, so the switch removes that attribute with the feature's
`cfg`s.

The retirement at the switch removes the module's six `equiv` tests. Their map to the unit
tests that keep what each established is the run dir's `equiv-retirement.md`. Five new
`unit_pub` tests, and new cases in four others, keep what none kept: the versions 0.9, 1.0, 1.1 and 2.0 for keep-alive
(`http_0_9_…`, `http_1_0_…`, `http_1_1_…`, and `http_2_0_is_read_as_an_earlier_version_for_keep_alive`
for the departure), a skipped chunked body upgrading, an unsettled parser never refused
(`after_headers_complete_on_a_zeroed_parser_s_rarer_states`), the unused flag bits, a 199, a 304
with a length, a 101 with no upgrade header or `Upgrade` alone, a `CONNECT` with a body, and the start
line's fields kept by `after_message_complete`. What no test keeps, and none needs once the C is
gone: the byte-for-byte differential over the private fields, and the bytes no safe path and no C
stores (an unnamed type or method, an upgrade byte of 2).

Gates, at 24 to 32 jobs, without BSan (the settings' `sanitizers` answer). On the tip `a81dc3103`
(`end-gates` snapshot), plain passes the whole workspace (`lib` 903 and 1 ignored, `equiv` 538,
`ub_safe` 798, `ub_unsafe` 144, `unit_pub` 230, `hidden_symbols` 1, doctests 106 and 397).
ASan+UBSan and TSan pass it but for the known nightly failures, the 9 `compile_fail` snapshots
and the `CommitBuilder` doctest, with no sanitizer report. Miri passes every binary (`lib` 443,
`equiv` 38, `ub_safe` 213, `unit_pub` 148, `ub_unsafe` 26 passed, the rest marked). The tip's
lint failure is the finding above. On this tree, `fmt --all --check` and `clippy --workspace
--all-targets -D warnings` pass, feature off and on, and so does the new `end-gates --stages
lint` over it. The fix changes only the `unit_pub` and `equiv` binaries, which pass on plain,
ASan+UBSan and TSan (`unit_pub` 235, `equiv` 538), and under Miri (`unit_pub` 149, `equiv` 38,
the rest marked). The five new tests marked `calls C` were each run alone under Miri and stop at
`llhttp__internal_init`. `equiv`'s rewritten fixture runs clean under Miri up to its first hook.

The link check, as the task message asked and the switch will have it. Private builds under
`crustify/tmp/linkcheck/<variant>` copy `libcrustify.a` without `deps/llhttp/http.c.o`, the
archive's second `http.c.o` member (`ar dN 2`; 209 objects, `nm` showing

and clippy passes with warnings denied. ASan+UBSan and TSan pass it but for the known
failures, with no sanitizer report. Their runs took this tree's `unit_pub` before its

without `deps/llhttp/CMakeFiles/llhttp.dir/http.c.o`, with the crate built as a `staticlib`
with the feature on. They define the four exports and no `llhttp_message_needs_eof`.
`crustify/scripts/http-gate.sh` ran over them on plain, ASan+UBSan and TSan. Each `results.txt`
is identical to batch 0's, and so to the one api.c's switch recorded over gen3's C: every clone,
failure, suite tally and request alike, with no sanitizer report. On TSan it is also identical
to the stock gen3 `tsan` variant's own run.

run-to-run noise. Worklist: `http.rs` 94 of 94 lines, 12 of 12 functions and 111 of 111 regions,
under the unit column alone too, the gateway compiled out. The safety audit scan (ffimap
`9aa2ef1`, flags as batch 0's, the export feature on) differs from batch 0's only in test
counters (`code.tests.loc.total` `+101`, which the Overview takes). `ffimap api` (nightly
`2026-10-08`, ffibox's with private items; the library's sources are the tip's, so one rustdoc
JSON serves both sides): the 5 items and the 24 unattributed modules `kept`. No raw binding or
C changed, so the packaging gate does not apply. The `+unit` cell counts the five new
`unit_pub` tests.

This pass changed `end-gates`, as its role evolves `testing-gates`: a `lint` stage runs the
format check and the lints over the snapshot's commit, once per feature set
(`crustify/evolution/end-gates-lint-stage`, crustify `28a5e51` on its evolution branch, awaiting
review). Usage cells are the assistant's.

### `git2/src/cli/opt.c` integration: the switch from C

The campaign's second switch, and the first of the `git2` link unit, the CLI. It was run by
`modules/git2/src/cli/opt.c/integration/run-1` on the module's branch, after the merge of the
working branch (`6d823f4d7`): `f68ea8660`, and the fork's `f57e1a616`. It followed
`utf8.c`'s procedure (`crustify/evolution/module-switch-procedure`) with its scripts unchanged.
The export feature `ffi-export-src-cli-opt-c` is deleted, so `opt.rs`'s gateway compiles from
now on, and its six `unit_priv` tests run in `lib`. No export feature is left. The CLI's
remaining C calls the five exports `cli_opt_parser_init`, `cli_opt_parser_next`,

entry='''### `libgit2/deps/llhttp/http.c` integration: the switch from C

The campaign's fourth switch, and llhttp's second, run by
`modules/libgit2/deps/llhttp/http.c/integration/run-1` on the module's branch, after the merge of
the working branch (`b478971b2`): `2e009d962`, and the fork's `230c9dbdb`. It followed api.c's
switch (`crustify/evolution/module-switch-procedure`) with its scripts, changing only the HTTP
gate's tally (below). The export feature `ffi-export-deps-llhttp-http-c` is deleted, so `http.rs`'s
gateway compiles from now on, and its four `unit_priv` tests run in `lib`. No export feature is
left. The module pass's warning held: `headers_code` carried a second mention of the feature,
`cfg_attr(not(any(test, feature = …)), expect(dead_code))`, which is removed with the gateway's
`cfg`, since the gateway now calls it always. After the switch, no file of the crate names the
feature. The remaining C calls the four exports: `llhttp.c`'s generated parser the three hooks,
`llhttp__before_headers_complete`, `llhttp__after_headers_complete` and
`llhttp__after_message_complete`, and libgit2's HTTP client `llhttp_should_keep_alive`, through
`httpparser.h`'s `git_http_parser_keep_alive`, which `httpclient.c`'s `on_headers_complete`
expands. The raw binding of `llhttp_should_keep_alive` stays and reaches its export. That of
`llhttp_message_needs_eof`, which has no export and which only http.c's C and its equivalence
tests called, goes with its allowlist entry, and `bindings.rs` was regenerated without it
(against gen4, whose headers the switch does not change). This changes the crate's raw API,
`sys::libgit2`; the safe API does not change. The hooks have no header declaration and no raw
binding. `deps/llhttp/http.c` leaves `c/` on the local `fork/main` as `integrate
deps/llhttp/http.c`, which is not pushed. `llhttp.h` stays for `llhttp.c` and the HTTP client.
`deps/llhttp/CMakeLists.txt` is unchanged; its `set_source_files_properties` now names two
removed files, `api.c` and `http.c`, and CMake ignores both. The module has no tied C test.

The module's six `equiv` tests are retired with the C they compared (`tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/http.rs`

`deps/llhttp/http.c` has switched from C to Rust. Two commits are on `crustify/modules/libgit2/deps/llhttp/http.c` on top of `b478971b2`, the tip is `46055d7c3`, and nothing was pushed. Every gate passed apart from the known nightly failures, and nothing is blocked.

**Commits**
- **`2e009d962` `http.c: switch from C to Rust (…/integration/run-1)`**:
  - The feature `ffi-export-deps-llhttp-http-c` is deleted, so the gateway compiles from now on. `headers_code`'s `cfg_attr` that named the feature is removed too, and no file in `src`, `tests`, `Cargo.toml`, `build.rs` or `sys` names it any more.
  - `tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/http.rs` and its `mod` line are retired. All six tests call C, so none is carried over.
  - `llhttp_message_needs_eof`'s allowlist entry is gone, and `bindings.rs` was regenerated against gen4. `llhttp_should_keep_alive`'s binding stays.
  - The submodule points at the fork's `230c9dbdb`, `integrate deps/llhttp/http.c`, a commit on the local `fork/main` that only removes the file.
- **`46055d7c3`**: the dashboard's Notes entry, items 14 to 17 added to `module-switch-procedure`, the HTTP gate change below, and this run dir's `task.json`, `task.md` and `http-gate-results.txt`.

**Variants**
- gen5 is built at `crustify/builds.gen5` (five variants, 12 jobs each, about 6 minutes), and this worktree's `crustify/builds` links to it. gen4 was not touched.
- Each archive holds 209 objects where gen4's held 210. `nm -A` confirms llhttp's `http.c.o` is the one that left: the remaining one defines only `git_smart_subtransport_http`.
- Every `libgit2.so`, `git2` and `libgit2_tests` defines the four exports and no `llhttp_message_needs_eof`.
- The earlier switches' smoke suite, `util_tests -sutf8`, no longer exists since wave 232, so I smoke-tested with `-sstr` and `git2 --version`.

**Gates** (all on gen5)
- **Format and lints:** fmt (nightly) and clippy with warnings denied are clean.
- **Workspace tests:** plain passes everything (`lib` 907, `equiv` 532, `ub_safe` 798, `ub_unsafe` 144, `unit_pub` 236, doctests 106 and 397). ASan/UBSan and TSan fail only the 9 `compile_fail` snapshots and the `CommitBuilder` doctest, with no sanitizer report.
- **Miri:** passes every test binary, the gateway's four tests included.
- **C tests (`c-tests.sh`):** each variant matches `c-baseline.json` (plain, ASan/UBSan and TSan 3442 of 3497, coverage 3443). Under TSan, `ctest offline` fails only on the baseline's own 49 lock-order inversions and glibc's `tzset` race, with no Rust frame in any report.
- **Packaging:** the crate packages (694 files) and builds alone in bundled mode. Its `lib` tests pass 849. The other 58 fail because the fixture repositories under `c/tests/resources` are not packaged, the same count as at api.c's switch.
- **HTTP gate:** gen4 (C) and gen5 (Rust) give the same `results.txt` on plain, ASan/UBSan and TSan, and gen5's coverage variant gives it too. On the coverage variant the run calls all four exports.
- **BSan:** rebuilt as a variant and not run, as instructed.

**One change beyond the procedure.** `http-gate.sh` only counted requests, so it could not catch a broken `llhttp_should_keep_alive`: a client that stopped reusing connections sends the same requests. I made `http-remote.py` log each request's position on its connection, and `http-gate.sh` now also counts the connections opened per framing, after the request lines, which are unchanged. Four gen4 runs gave identical counts, and gen5 matches them. I did not build a broken export to prove the new count catches one.

**Proposed, not made** (evidence in `module-switch-procedure`):
- **Item 14:** deleting a feature should remove every mention of its name, not just the gateway's `cfg`.
- **Item 15:** archive member names are not unique, so the check that a file left should go by its symbols or object path.
- **Item 16:** the connection count above. This one is made, in the campaign's scripts only.
- **Item 17:** the variants' smoke suite should be named once, from C that stays.

No review reproducer names the deleted feature.

**After the rebase.** This run had no rebase and no landing lock: you merged at `b478971b2` and I only committed on top, so every gate above ran on the final tree. The records commit changes only the dashboard, the proposal, the run dir and the two HTTP scripts. None of the Rust or C gates depend on those, so their results hold for `46055d7c3`. The HTTP results come from the changed scripts.

I removed my scratch from `crustify/tmp`. The logs already there before I started are still there, and none of my processes is running.
